text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Newspaper says billions of lek have arrived in Albania from Malta, alleging the new bank notes have been printed to pay President Sali Berisha's supporters during planned June elections. It claims the finance minister, a Socialist Party representative, has not been informed about the issue.
- Council of Europe and European Parliament will send 90 observers to join the OSCE's 400-strong group of monitors for the June 29 elections.
- Socialist Party asked Premier Bashkim Fino to take under his control special police units which it said are still controlled by the Democratic Party.
- Italian Defence undersecretary Massimo Brutti is quoted as saying international instutions would compensate for the money thousands of Albanians lost in pyramid investment schemes.
- The paper alleges that many people attending President Berisha's election rallies are members of his republican guards.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Paper says OSCE coordinator Brian Pridham did not resign for "personal reasons", but in protest over the European countries' alleged decision to fix the outcome of early elections.
- All Albanian politicians should be held responsible for the crisis which has hit the country, prominent writer Ismail Kadare is quoted as telling Italian daily Corriere della Sera.
- Four workers were burned alive in a plant in central town of Elbasan.

- The Italian Communist Refoundation party called for an inquiry into Italian diplomatic and financial involvement in Albania, alleging that suspect dealings may have worsened the situation in Albania.
ALBANIA
- We are called on June 29 to give the right answer to communism, President Sali Berisha told a crowd of supporters in the town of Kruje.
- Local court in Durres hands out a prison sentence for a man accused of trying to kill President Sali Berisha by hurling a grenade at him while he was holding an electoral campaign speech last week.

- An opinion poll by the EUREKA institute shows that the Union for Democracy, an alliance of the Democratic Party and several centrist and rightest parties, will win over 50 percent of votes in the planned June 29 elections.
INDIPENDENT
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano held rallies in southern Albania where thousands of people poured out to show their support for the leftist leader.
- The U.S. favour free and democratic elections in Albania and will back a coalition government, the assistant to State Secretary Rudolph Perina said in interview.
- President Sali Berisha has finally turned down a request by the International Monetary Fund for more transparency in the pyramid investment scheme issue.
